explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/379: S(n) is the largest integer such that for all 1 ≤ k < n, C(n,k) is divisible by p^{S(n)} for some prime p depending on k; is limsup S(n) = ∞? (solved affirmatively by Cambie, Kovač and Tao). In Lean S n = sSup {s | ∀ k ∈ [1,n), ∃ prime p, p^s ∣ C(n,k)}; for n ≥ 2 the set contains 0, is downward closed and bounded (k = 1 forces p^s ∣ n), so sSup is the intended maximum; for n ≤ 1 the set is all of ℕ and sSup gives the junk value 0, which does not affect the limsup. The statement limsup (S n : ℕ∞) = ⊤ is exactly limsup S(n) = ∞, stated as the (known) positive answer. Faithful.
